record.original_question: For multiprocessor scheduling of sporadic task systems whose task parameters C_i, D_i, and T_i are all positive integers, determine whether the Integer Boundary Constraint holds. That is, is a sporadic task system feasible on a multiprocessor platform under continuous preemptive scheduling if and only if, for every legal sequence of job arrivals, there exists a discrete schedule that divides time into indivisible time slots and assigns tasks to slots while meeting all deadlines?

evidence.quote: Suppose that all task parameters – the Ci’s, Di’s, and Ti’s – of a sporadic task system are specified as positive integers.
A discrete schedule assumes that the time-line is divided into indivisible time-lots, and specifies the tasks scheduled during each time-slot.

Problem 5 (Does the Integer Boundary Constraint (IBC) hold for multiprocessors?) Is it true that a sporadic task system is multiprocessor feasible if and only if it has a discrete schedule for every sequence of job arrivals?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a sporadic task system τ = {τ_1, …, τ_n} to be scheduled on a platform of m identical processors. Each task τ_i is specified by a triple (C_i, D_i, T_i) of positive integers, where C_i is the worst-case execution requirement, D_i is the relative deadline, and T_i is the minimum inter-arrival separation. Each task τ_i generates a (possibly infinite) sequence of jobs; successive jobs of τ_i are released at least T_i time units apart, each job requires up to C_i units of execution, and each job released at time t must complete by time t + D_i. A legal sequence of job arrivals is any sequence consistent with these constraints.

Under continuous preemptive scheduling on m processors, time is treated as a continuum: at any instant, each processor may execute at most one job, each job may execute on at most one processor, and preemption and migration are permitted at arbitrary real-valued time instants. The system τ is said to be (multiprocessor) feasible if for every legal sequence of job arrivals there exists a continuous preemptive schedule on m processors that meets every deadline.

A discrete schedule partitions the non-negative time line into unit-length, indivisible slots [k, k+1), k ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, and assigns to each slot, for each processor, at most one job of τ; the constraints that no job runs on two processors in the same slot and that a job receives at most C_i slots of execution within each window [r, r+D_i) (where r is its release time) must be respected, and every job must complete by its deadline.

Question (Integer Boundary Constraint for multiprocessors): Is it true that, for every sporadic task system τ with integer parameters and every integer m ≥ 1, τ is multiprocessor feasible under continuous preemptive scheduling on m processors if and only if, for every legal sequence of job arrivals (with integer release times), there exists a discrete schedule on m processors that meets all deadlines?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published resolution of the Integer Boundary Constraint question for multiprocessor sporadic task systems. Surveys of multiprocessor real-time scheduling continue to list feasibility-related questions (e.g., absence of a known finite collection of worst-case arrival sequences for global scheduling) as open, but no source was located that explicitly proves or disproves the IBC for multiprocessors. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: A Survey of Hard Real-Time Scheduling for Multiprocessor Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys multiprocessor real-time scheduling and notes ongoing open questions in feasibility analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Feasibility-related questions for multiprocessor sporadic task systems remain among the open problems in the field.

status_evidence.title: Feasibility Analysis of Sporadic Real-Time Multiprocessor Task Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Develops feasibility tests for sporadic real-time multiprocessor task systems but does not state a resolution of the Integer Boundary Constraint.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution of the multiprocessor IBC is reported.
